purpose: Independently review semantic contrast expectations before the prospective development diagnostic. These fictional examples are not admitted historical news and are not claimed as completed model tests.
source_policy: The supplied fictional records stipulate their described provenance; no outside facts, later outcomes or real entities are needed.

cases.material: Desk note: Mira alleged that the amber lamp had three bulbs. The desk has not inspected the lamp and has no other evidence of its bulb count.
cases.target: The desk note records Mira alleging that the amber lamp had three bulbs.
cases.reason: This exact attribution is directly recorded. The underlying bulb count need not be established to support this target.

cases.material: Desk note: Mira alleged that the amber lamp had three bulbs. The desk has not inspected the lamp and has no other evidence of its bulb count.
cases.target: The amber lamp had three bulbs.
cases.reason: The same record establishes only an expressly unverified allegation. Missing inspection does not establish the opposite bulb count.

cases.material: Contemporaneous public meeting record, stipulated authentic and complete for this fictional example: the clerk directly witnessed chair Neri open the meeting at the recorded time. No second observer account is supplied.
cases.target: Chair Neri opened the meeting at the time recorded by the clerk.
cases.reason: The stipulated adequate first-hand record directly supports this narrow occurrence. A second account is optional, not a missing necessary premise.

cases.material: On day 1, a planning note estimated that the blue booth would sell nine tickets on day 2. At the day-3 evidence cutoff, no completed sales record is supplied.
cases.target: The day-1 planning note estimated nine ticket sales for the blue booth on day 2.
cases.reason: The target preserves the source's estimate modality.

cases.material: On day 1, a planning note estimated that the blue booth would sell nine tickets on day 2. At the day-3 evidence cutoff, no completed sales record is supplied.
cases.target: The blue booth actually sold nine tickets on day 2.
cases.reason: The earlier forecast does not establish the realized count. The occurrence is unresolved rather than contradicted.

cases.material: The supplied authenticated register exhaustively records all ballots in this fictional count: two amber ballots and three violet ballots; these are disjoint categories and there are no other ballots.
cases.target: There were six ballots in the fictional count.
cases.reason: The explicit exhaustive, disjoint counts give two plus three equals five. This excludes six without assuming hidden categories.

cases.material: Bulletin A repeats Mira's unverified allegation that the amber lamp had three bulbs. Bulletin B explicitly quotes A and has conducted no separate inspection. A and B provide no additional evidence about the lamp itself.
cases.target: The amber lamp had three bulbs.
cases.reason: The dependent retellings do not supply the missing underlying evidence. The result is not unresolved merely because the sources share an origin.

cases.material: The fictional inventory has been directly checked and is stipulated complete: tray A contains two cards, tray B contains four different cards, and these are the only cards. A note states that the combined inventory has six cards.
cases.target: The combined fictional inventory has six cards.
cases.reason: The explicit complete disjoint inventory independently permits the stated sum; the answer need not stop at the note's assertion.

revision_basis: Only s07 names the same lamp explicitly, isolating dependence without an extra identity gap. All other fixtures and expected labels remain unchanged.
